content:
You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- Final answer format. First list the passages you rely on, copied VERBATIM from the files (no
  paraphrase, no ellipsis inside the quotation marks), then write the answer using only them:
  <evidence>
  [E1] "exact text" (file)
  [E2] "exact text" (file)
  </evidence>
  <answer>
  Your answer to the user. End every factual sentence with the evidence it rests on, e.g. [E1] or
  [E1, E2]. A statement that the document(s) do not contain the requested information needs no marker.
  </answer>
- The user sees only the <answer> part, so it must be complete and readable on its own.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- After you give an answer, an automatic check verifies your citations. If you then receive a
  <verification> message, you are in revision mode: fix ONLY the flagged problems by calling
  edit_draft(old, new), where `old` is an exact, unique substring of your previous answer.
  Keep everything else unchanged, and reply "Done" when finished.
  Never call edit_draft before you have given an answer.

Summarize this document into easily executable bullet points.

In your answer, refer only to the document in the file `doc.txt`. Do not employ any outside knowledge.

1	Week 1, Day 1
     2	What you will see first is the Adventure Screen. This is where you will spend a great deal of
     3	time while playing Heroes III. The main window provides you with a close view around your
     4	heroes and cities, while the world map (located in the upper-right corner of the screen) shows
     5	you a small view of the entire world. Notice that most of the world map is black – that is
     6	because until you send a hero to explore an area you won’t know what is there. Don’t worry
     7	about any of the other buttons below the World Map, these will be described in greater detail
     8	later.
     9	Your first hero, Lord Haart, should already be selected (he’s sitting on his horse, waiting for
    10	instructions). The first thing we’ll want him to do is visit the town, so place your mouse cursor
    11	over the entrance to the town (between the two flag poles). Notice how the horse icon rears up
    12	on its hind legs – this means that by traveling to that location, your hero will interact with
    13	whatever is there. Also, the name and a short description of the location appears in the Rollover
    14	Bar at the bottom of the screen (the rollover bar appears on nearly every screen in Heroes III and
    15	gives useful, context sensitive information). When you click on a location, a set of green arrows
    16	show the path your hero will take to reach the large green X. It is this X that marks your hero’s
    17	destination. Click again on the same location and your hero will move to the castle (a fast way to
    18	move is to simply double click on an intended destination – the first click selects the path, the
    19	second click sends the hero). When the hero arrives at the entrance to the town, the view will
    20	change to the Town Screen.
    21	Town Screen
    22	This is the Town Screen for the Castle town type (there are eight different town types in Heroes
    23	III, each with its own unique creatures and buildings). Most of this screen is taken up by the
    24	town view. Any structures or upgrades you build in this town will appear here. As you can see,
    25	several structures have already been constructed. Specific information about the town is
    26	displayed in the bottom-left corner of the screen, including town income (per day) and troop
    27	production (per week). To the right of the town info are two rows of boxes. The top row is for
    28	any troops that are currently in the town’s garrison, the bottom row is for any troops currently
    29	visiting a town with a hero.
    30	The first thing you will want to do is build a Fort. To do so, click on the larger of the two
    31	buildings on the left side of the town view – the Town Hall – to enter the Hall Screen.
    32	The Hall Screen is where you make all your construction decisions. Any building you can
    33	currently build is shown with its name in a green bar. Any building that you can not build, but
    34	can be built later is shown with its name in a red bar. If a building has been disabled or can
    35	never be built, its name will appear in a gray bar. Once you have completely built or upgraded a
    36	structure as high as it will go, its name will be displayed in gold.
    37	Click on the picture of the Fort. You will be shown a description of what the Fort does, as well
    38	as what resources are required to build it. Click on the Build button (in the lower left hand
    39	corner of the popup window) and the Fort will be constructed.
    40	Now that you have a Fort, click on it to view the Castle Window. This window shows you
    41	information about all seven units that can be produced by this town. Any troop-producing
    42	structures (usually referred to as Creature Generators) that are already constructed will show a
    43	number of Available units (currently the Guardhouse, Archers’ Tower, and Barracks show units
    44	available – the other structures have not been built yet). Click the Exit button (lower right) to
    45	return to the Town Screen.
    46	The round tower on the right side of the screen is your Mage Guild. It is here that heroes go to
    47	learn the spells that they will cast while adventuring. Click on the Mage Guild, then choose to
    48	buy a spell book. Since Lord Haart is a Knight, he does not begin with a spell book. All heroes
    49	must have a spell book before they can learn or cast spells. Once you agree to purchase a spell
    50	book, you are shown the Mage Guild Screen. Each of the spells the Mage Guild offers is listed
    51	on scrolls on the various shelves in the guild. Left or right clicking on any spell scroll will show
    52	you a description of that spell. When you are ready to leave, click on the Exit button (lower
    53	right).
    54	Your hero starts with troops, but it’s really just a token force, so you should buy any available
    55	troops and add them to his army. Along the hill at the back of your town are three towers. Click
    56	on the large central tower. The Recruit Pikemen window is displayed. Using the scroll bar you
    57	can select how many troops you wish to purchase, and the total cost is calculated to the right.
    58	However, the fastest way to buy troops is to use the Maximum button (the four up arrows at the
    59	bottom of the popup window) which will automatically calculate the maximum number of troops
    60	available that you can currently afford. Click the Maximum button, then click the Recruit button
    61	(bottom center). Notice how there are now Pikemen in the garrison row of your town.

Also, the name and a short description of the location appears in the Rollover Bar at the bottom of the screen (the rollover bar appears on nearly every screen in Heroes III and gives useful, context sensitive information). When you click on a location, a set of green arrows show the path your hero will take to reach the large green X. It is this X that marks your hero’s destination. Click again on the same location and your hero will move to the castle (a fast way to move is to simply double click on an intended destination – the first click selects the path, the second click sends the hero). When the hero arrives at the entrance to the town, the view will change to the Town Screen." (doc.txt)
[E4] "This is the Town Screen for the Castle town type (there are eight different town types in Heroes III, each with its own unique creatures and buildings). Most of this screen is taken up by the town view. Any structures or upgrades you build in this town will appear here. As you can see, several structures have already been constructed. Specific information about the town is displayed in the bottom-left corner of the screen, including town income (per day) and troop production (per week). To the right of the town info are two rows of boxes. The top row is for any troops that are currently in the town’s garrison, the bottom row is for any troops currently visiting a town with a hero." (doc.txt)
[E5] "The first thing you will want to do is build a Fort. To do so, click on the larger of the two buildings on the left side of the town view – the Town Hall – to enter the Hall Screen. The Hall Screen is where you make all your construction decisions. Any building you can currently build is shown with its name in a green bar. Any building that you can not build, but can be built later is shown with its name in a red bar. If a building has been disabled or can never be built, its name will appear in a gray bar. Once you have completely built or upgraded a structure as high as it will go, its name will be displayed in gold. Click on the picture of the Fort. You will be shown a description of what the Fort does, as well as what resources are required to build it. Click on the Build button (in the lower left hand corner of the popup window) and the Fort will be constructed." (doc.txt)
[E6] "Now that you have a Fort, click on it to view the Castle Window. This window shows you information about all seven units that can be produced by this town. Any troop-producing structures (usually referred to as Creature Generators) that are already constructed will show a number of Available units (currently the Guardhouse, Archers’ Tower, and Barracks show units available – the other structures have not been built yet). Click on the Mage Guild, then choose to buy a spell book. Since Lord Haart is a Knight, he does not begin with a spell book. All heroes must have a spell book before they can learn or cast spells. Once you agree to purchase a spell book, you are shown the Mage Guild Screen. Each of the spells the Mage Guild offers is listed on scrolls on the various shelves in the guild. However, the fastest way to buy troops is to use the Maximum button (the four up arrows at the bottom of the popup window) which will automatically calculate the maximum number of troops available that you can currently afford. <answer>
**Week 1, Day 1 — executable steps** (from doc.txt)

**On the Adventure Screen**
- Note the layout: the main window gives a close view around your heroes and cities; the world map in the upper-right corner shows a small view of the entire world, and most of it is black until you send a hero to explore an area [E2].
- Confirm your first hero, Lord Haart, is selected (he is sitting on his horse, waiting for instructions) [E3].
- Move the mouse cursor over the town entrance (between the two flag poles); the horse icon rearing up on its hind legs means the hero will interact with that location, and the location's name and short description appear in the Rollover Bar at the bottom of the screen [E3].
- Click the location: green arrows show the path to the large green X, which marks the destination; click the same location again to send the hero (fastest: double-click the destination — first click selects the path, second click sends the hero) [E3].
- When the hero arrives at the town entrance, the view changes to the Town Screen [E3].

**On the Town Screen (Castle town type)**
- Understand the screen: the town view shows any structures or upgrades you build; the bottom-left corner shows town income (per day) and troop production (per week); the top row of boxes on the right is the town's garrison troops, and the bottom row is troops currently visiting with a hero [E4].
- Build a Fort: click the Town Hall (the larger of the two buildings on the left side of the town view) to enter the Hall Screen, where all construction decisions are made [E5].
- In the Hall Screen, read the color coding: green bar = building you can currently build; red bar = not buildable now but buildable later; gray bar = disabled or can never be built; gold = completely built or upgraded as high as it will go [E5].
- Click the picture of the Fort to see its description and required resources, then click the Build button (lower-left corner of the popup window) to construct it [E5].
- After the Fort is built, click it to open the Castle Window, which shows information about all seven units the town can produce; already-constructed Creature Generators (currently the Guardhouse, Archers' Tower, and Barracks) show a number of Available units; click Exit (lower right) to return to the Town Screen [E6].
- Buy a spell book: click the round tower on the right (the Mage Guild), then choose to buy a spell book — Lord Haart is a Knight and does not begin with one, and all heroes must have a spell book before they can learn or cast spells [E7].
- On the Mage Guild Screen, spells are listed on scrolls on the shelves; left- or right-click any spell scroll to see its description; click Exit (lower right) to leave [E7].
- Recruit troops: the hero's starting troops are only a token force, so buy available troops and add them to his army [E8].
- Click the large central tower (of the three towers along the hill at the back of the town) to open the Recruit Pikemen window [E8].
- Either use the scroll bar to select a number of troops (total cost is calculated to the right), or, for the fastest purchase, click the Maximum button (the four up arrows at the bottom of the popup) to auto-select the maximum number you can currently afford [E8].
- Click the Recruit button (bottom center); the new Pikemen then appear in the garrison row of your town [E8].
</answer>
